content.text: The blockchain does not have a map of restricted countries. A wallet address in Lagos processes a transaction identically to one in London. USDT moves from a buyer in Manila to a seller in Harare in under 60 seconds — no correspondent bank, no SWIFT delay, no compliance officer deciding whether the corridor is permitted. This is the operational reality that creators across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, and the Philippines are using right now to sell digital products to a global audience. The [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage|infrastructure]] exists. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages serves the storefront. The product delivers before the buyer closes their wallet. The only question is whether you have assembled the stack correctly.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

By using a combination of Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, Supabase, Google Drive, and NOWPayments, you can create a payment and delivery pipeline that's entirely self-sufficient. This means you can process transactions without relying on Stripe or PayPal, and deliver your products without worrying about platform downtime or restrictions. The result is a fully sovereign digital commerce stack that's tailored to the unique needs of Zimbabwean creators.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack, you'll need to set up a few essential components. These include a domain name, a Cloudflare account, a Supabase account, a Google Drive account, and a NOWPayments account. You'll also need to choose a cryptocurrency to use for payments, such as USDT on Tron or Binance Coin. With these components in place, you'll be ready to deploy your stack and start selling digital products globally.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to create a Cloudflare Worker that integrates with NOWPayments. This will enable you to process payments in real-time and deliver your products to customers. You'll also need to set up a Supabase database to store customer information and order details. With these components in place, you'll have a fully functional payment and delivery pipeline that's entirely self-sufficient.
Sovereign digital commerce stacks are designed to be highly adaptable and can be used in a variety of different contexts.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you're ready to go live and process your first transaction. To do this, you'll need to deploy your Cloudflare Worker and Supabase database to a production environment. You'll also need to configure your NOWPayments account to accept payments in your chosen cryptocurrency. With these steps complete, you'll be able to process your first transaction and start selling digital products globally.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your digital commerce business grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to keep up with demand. To do this, you can use Cloudflare's built-in scaling features to automatically adjust your capacity as needed. You can also use Supabase to set up load balancing and caching to improve performance. With these strategies in place, you'll be able to scale your infrastructure to meet the needs of your growing business.

Choose a cryptocurrency to use for payments. Set up a NOWPayments account and integrate it with your Cloudflare Worker. Deploy your Cloudflare Worker and Supabase database to a production environment. Configure your NOWPayments account to accept payments in your chosen cryptocurrency. Test your payment and delivery pipeline to ensure it's working correctly.
